column1: # comment: "Mentation slice alignments \u2014 the occurrent (perdurant) half of mind. AXIOMATIC PARENT (not a mapping row): gmeow:MentalProcess rdfs:subClassOf gmeow:Event, and gmeow:Event is grounded in gUFO's gufo:Event \u2014 the gUFO Event axiom is imported transitively via the events slice, not as a mapping row. EXTERNAL BRIDGES NAMED IN PROSE (no stable, resolvable RDF namespace available): * Cognitive Atlas (cognitiveatlas.org): 'cognitive process' and 'mental process' concepts (e.g. reasoning, perception, attention, imagery) closely match the gmeow:MentalProcessType value vocabulary; the Cognitive Atlas uses ad-hoc numeric IRIs inside an undeclared namespace and no OWL-resolvable ontology file, so no TermEquivalence row can be written \u2014 the conceptual alignment is documented here instead. * Cognitive Paradigm Ontology (cpo, cogpo.org): maps cognitive tasks and paradigms to mental constructs; broadly aligns with the gmeow:MentalProcessType seed vocabulary but exposes no stable OWL-resolvable namespace for term-level alignment. * Mental Functioning Ontology (MFOEM, purl.obolibrary.org/obo/mfoem.owl): provides a BFO-based taxonomy of mental processes; BFO_0000015 ('process') is the closest alignable IRI (see the mapping row below); MFOEM's finer-grained mental process subclasses (e.g. MFOEM:MentalProcess) are not resolvable as stable IRIs in the OBO Foundry published OWL and are therefore named in prose only. * SUMO (ontologyportal.org): IntentionalProcess and Reasoning are conceptually adjacent to gmeow:MentalProcess and gmeow:processReasoning; the SUMO OWL serialization IRIs (ontologyportal.org/SUMO.owl#...) are not resolvable over HTTPS, so SUMO alignments are named in prose here rather than as TermEquivalence rows."
# # No frame-selecting mapping (Principle 9): GMEOW does not assert a single 'correct' mental process taxonomy; value-vocab members are co-equal.

column6: a mental process is a process (BFO_0000015: a occurrent that has some temporal proper part and is not a temporal region); loose match — BFO process is very broad and does not imply an experiencer
